discovered.0: The box was left blank or the information was not available, so the report does not say how the defect was found and nothing should be concluded from that.
discovered.9: The filer did not know how the defect was found, so treat this as missing information rather than evidence of anything.
discovered.B: The defect was seen inside an enclosed space such as an engine, using a borescope, a long thin camera passed in through a small opening so the inside can be checked without taking it apart.
discovered.C: The defect was found while running or testing the system to see whether it works, rather than by looking at it.
discovered.D: A dye was applied to the surface and drawn into any cracks, then made visible, so this method finds cracks that open onto the surface.
discovered.L: The defect was found by visual inspection with a light, such as a flashlight, illuminating the area.
discovered.M: The part was magnetized and coated with iron particles that gather at flaws, a way of finding cracks in metal.
discovered.O: None of the listed methods fit; the narrative should say how the defect was actually found, and this code by itself is not evidence of anything.
discovered.T: The defect was found with a thermal camera that shows heat patterns, so the problem appeared as an abnormal temperature.
discovered.U: The defect was found by ultrasound, sound waves passed through the part that can reveal flaws hidden inside it.
discovered.W: The defect was found by looking at it closely under magnification, such as through a magnifying glass.
discovered.X: The defect was found by x-ray, which shows the inside of a part without cutting it open.

stage.00: The box was left blank or the information was not available, so the report does not say what the aircraft was doing and nothing should be concluded from that.
stage.AA: The aircraft was flying an air ambulance mission, carrying patients or medical personnel.
stage.AB: The aircraft was flying aerobatics, deliberate manoeuvres such as rolls and loops.
stage.AG: The aircraft was doing agricultural work, such as spraying crops.
stage.AP: The aircraft was descending toward a runway to land.
stage.CR: The aircraft was in cruise, the steady level part of the flight between climb and descent.
stage.EX: The aircraft was carrying a load attached to the outside, such as a load slung under a helicopter.
stage.FF: The aircraft was fighting a fire, for example by dropping water or retardant.
stage.HO: The aircraft was hovering, holding a fixed position in the air, which applies to helicopters.
stage.IN: The aircraft was on the ground being inspected or worked on, so the defect turned up during maintenance rather than in flight.
stage.MS: The aircraft was flying a mapping or survey mission, following a set pattern to photograph or measure the ground.
stage.NR: The filer did not report what the aircraft was doing, so treat this as missing information rather than evidence of anything.
stage.TX: The aircraft was moving on the ground under its own power, or being towed or pushed.
stage.UK: The filer did not know what the aircraft was doing when the defect appeared.

nature.0: The box was left blank or the information was not available, so the report does not describe the condition and nothing should be concluded from that.
nature.A: Fire or flames were seen or indicated.
nature.B: Smoke, fumes, an odour, or sparks were noticed.
nature.C: The damage was caused by a foreign object, something that does not belong there, such as debris struck or sucked into an engine.
nature.D: A part came off the aircraft while it was in flight.
nature.E: There was vibration or buffeting, meaning a shaking that can come from machinery or from airflow over the aircraft.
nature.F: The flight controls, the surfaces and linkages the pilot uses to steer the aircraft, were affected.
nature.G: More than one thing failed at the same time.
nature.H: Half of the aircraft's electrical power was lost.
nature.I: The instruments that show the aircraft's attitude, meaning whether it is pitched up or down and banked left or right, were affected.
nature.J: A warning light, message, or alarm indicated a problem.
nature.K: The aircraft was losing a fluid, such as fuel, oil, or hydraulic fluid.
nature.M: A temperature reading went above its limit.
nature.N: A warning appeared but did not reflect a real problem, so the faulty warning itself was the defect.
nature.O: The condition did not fit any listed category; the narrative should describe what actually happened, and this code by itself is not evidence of anything.
nature.P: The failure happened with no warning light or alert beforehand.
nature.S: The failure affected other systems besides the one that failed.
nature.W: The condition being reported was inadequate quality control, meaning the inspections and checks meant to catch defects were not done properly.
nature.X: The flame in an engine's combustion chamber went out in flight, so the engine stopped producing power.
nature.Z: The report is flagged as a significant failure, and the narrative should say what actually failed.

precaution.0: The box was left blank or the information was not available, so the report does not say what the crew did and nothing should be concluded from that.
precaution.A: The crew made a landing that was not planned, because of the problem.
precaution.B: The crew descended quickly, normally to reach a lower altitude, because of the problem.
precaution.C: The crew stopped the aircraft during the takeoff run instead of lifting off.
precaution.D: The aircraft went back to its parking position, such as the gate, rather than continuing.
precaution.E: The crew shut an engine down while the aircraft was in flight.
precaution.G: Oxygen masks dropped down or were otherwise deployed for use.
precaution.H: The crew switched off a system or an electrical circuit.
precaution.I: The cabin lost its pressurized air.
precaution.J: Fuel was released overboard in flight, generally to reduce the aircraft's weight before landing.
precaution.L: The crew broke off the approach and did not continue to land.
precaution.O: The crew took some other precaution not on this list; the narrative should say what, and this code by itself is not evidence of anything.

sdr_type.A: The report was filed by an air carrier, meaning an airline-type operator rather than a private flyer.
sdr_type.G: The report was filed under general aviation, which covers flying outside the airlines, such as private owners, small operators, and flight schools.
